one_line: An anonymous medieval Maru-Gurjara temple craftsman-architect shaping intricately carved stone shrines across western India.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s, lean craftsman’s build with strong forearms and calloused hands.
appearance.face: Oval face with sharp cheekbones, medium wheat complexion tanned from outdoor work, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache, a faint stone-dust scar on the left brow, default expression focused and quietly proud.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled back into a small low knot at the back of the head, front smoothed and center-parted; wrapped with a narrow off-white cotton headband tied at the right side to keep dust and sweat away.
appearance.costume: A calf-length, long-sleeved off-white cotton angarkha-style tunic crossing left over right and tied with inner and outer fabric ties, lightly stained with stone dust; beneath it a simple knee-length off-white dhoti wrapped securely and pleated in front; a narrow woven reddish-brown cotton patka (waist sash) with subtle darker stripes wrapped twice around the waist and knotted on the left, ends hanging to mid-thigh; a soft light-brown cotton shawl folded lengthwise and slung over the left shoulder and around the back for warmth or dust protection; simple dark leather sandals with thong straps; minimal jewellery limited to a slim copper bangle on the right wrist and a small round copper earring in the left ear to imply modest artisan status while remaining practical at a construction site.
appearance.signature: A polished, slightly worn mason’s mallet in his right hand with a dark wooden handle and pale stone head, paired with a chisel held delicately in his left hand, both tied at the waist when not in use.

ref_desc: A lean, tanned Maru-Gurjara shilpin in an off-white long-sleeved angarkha, off-white dhoti, reddish-brown waist sash, light-brown shawl, leather sandals, center-parted black hair in a low knot with a headband, copper accents, and a stone mallet and chisel in hand.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a Maru-Gurjara shilpin from 11th–13th century western India: a lean man in his early 30s with an oval, tanned face, sharp cheekbones, a straight nose, a neat moustache, and a slight scar above his left brow, his default expression focused and quietly proud. His thick black hair is center-parted, smoothed back into a small low knot, wrapped with a narrow off-white headband tied on the right. He wears a calf-length, long-sleeved off-white cotton angarkha-style tunic crossing left over right, lightly dusty from stone work, over an off-white dhoti wrapped to the knee. A woven reddish-brown cotton patka sash with subtle darker stripes is wrapped twice around his waist and knotted on the left, ends hanging to mid-thigh, and a soft light-brown cotton shawl is folded and draped over his left shoulder and around his back. On his wrist is a slim copper bangle and in his left ear a small round copper earring, and he wears dark brown leather thong sandals. In his hands he holds his signature tools: a polished stone-headed mason’s mallet with a dark wooden handle in his right hand and a matching chisel delicately in his left; show them clearly as his defining props. Use a muted palette of off-white for garments, reddish-brown for the sash, light brown for the shawl, dark brown for sandals and wood, and warm copper accents for jewellery and tool details, and present him from multiple angles to fix his face, hair, clothing, and tools consistently.
